title: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Radiation
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Formula for pressure exerted by an ideal gas in terms of rms speed?
cards.a: P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² = (1/3) (N m / V) v_rms², where N is total molecules, m is mass of one molecule, and V is volume.
cards.hint: Derived from rate of change of momentum of gas molecules colliding elastically with container walls.

cards.q: Formulas for RMS speed (v_rms) of gas molecules?
cards.a: v_rms = √(3 R T / M₀) = √(3 k_B T / m) = √(3 P / ρ), where M₀ is molar mass and k_B is Boltzmann constant.
cards.hint: v_rms ∝ √T and v_rms ∝ 1/√M₀. RMS speed depends strictly on absolute temperature and molar mass.

cards.q: Ratio of Most Probable, Average, and RMS speeds of gas molecules?
cards.a:
v_mp : v_avg : v_rms = √2 : √(8/π) : √3 ≈ 1 : 1.128 : 1.224.
Order: v_mp < v_avg < v_rms.
cards.hint: Mnemonic: 'RAM' (RMS > Average > Most probable).

cards.q: Kinetic Energy of an ideal gas per mole, per molecule, and per unit volume?
cards.a:
Per mole: E = (3/2) R T
Per molecule: E_molecule = (3/2) k_B T
Per unit volume: E / V = (3/2) P ⇒ P = (2/3) (E / V).
cards.hint: Pressure is numerically equal to two-thirds of the translational kinetic energy per unit volume!

cards.q: Mean Free Path λ of a gas molecule: Formula and dependencies?
cards.a: λ = 1 / (√2 π d² n_V) = (k_B T) / (√2 π d² P), where d is molecular diameter and n_V = N/V is number density.
cards.hint: λ ∝ T (at constant P); λ ∝ 1/P (at constant T); λ ∝ 1/d².

cards.q: Degrees of Freedom (f) for Monoatomic, Diatomic, and Triatomic gases?
cards.a:
Monoatomic (He, Ne, Ar): f = 3 (translational).
Diatomic rigid (H₂, O₂, N₂ at room temp): f = 5 (3 trans + 2 rot).
Diatomic non-rigid (high temp): f = 7 (3 trans + 2 rot + 2 vib).
Non-linear Triatomic (H₂O): f = 6 (3 trans + 3 rot).
cards.hint: Each vibrational mode contributes 2 degrees of freedom (1 kinetic + 1 potential).

cards.q: State the Law of Equipartition of Energy.
cards.a: In thermal equilibrium at absolute temperature T, total energy of gas is equally divided among all its degrees of freedom, and average energy per molecule per degree of freedom is (1/2) k_B T.
cards.hint: Total internal energy of one mole of gas with f degrees of freedom is U = (f/2) R T.

cards.q: Molar heat capacities C_v, C_p and adiabatic ratio γ in terms of degrees of freedom f?
cards.hint: Mayer's relation: C_p - C_v = R. Ratio γ is always greater than 1.

cards.q: Values of C_v, C_p, and γ for Monoatomic vs Diatomic gases?
cards.a:
Monoatomic (f = 3): C_v = (3/2)R, C_p = (5/2)R, γ = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.
Diatomic rigid (f = 5): C_v = (5/2)R, C_p = (7/2)R, γ = 7/5 = 1.40.
Diatomic vibrating (f = 7): C_v = (7/2)R, C_p = (9/2)R, γ = 9/7 ≈ 1.29.
cards.hint: Memorize 1.67, 1.40, and 1.29 — tested in nearly every MHT-CET physics paper!

cards.q: Mayer's Relation between Molar (C_p, C_v) and Principal (c_p, c_v) specific heats?
cards.a:
Molar specific heats: C_p - C_v = R (or R / J in heat units).
Principal specific heats: c_p - c_v = R / M₀, where M₀ is molar mass.
cards.hint: Principal specific heat is per unit mass (J/(kg·K)); Molar specific heat is per mole (J/(mol·K)).

cards.q: Absorptive, Reflective, and Transmissive powers: Relation and definition of a Blackbody?
cards.a:
a + r + t_r = 1 (where a = Q_a/Q, r = Q_r/Q, t_r = Q_t/Q).
For an opaque body: t_r = 0 ⇒ a + r = 1.
For a Perfectly Blackbody: a = 1, r = 0, t_r = 0.
cards.hint: A perfectly blackbody absorbs 100% of incident radiant energy of all wavelengths.

cards.q: Emissive power E and Emissivity (coefficient of emission) e?
cards.a:
Emissive Power: E = Q / (A · t) (radiant energy emitted per unit area per unit time). SI unit: J/(m²·s) or W/m².
Emissivity: e = E / E_b (ratio of emissive power to that of a perfectly blackbody at same temperature).
cards.hint: For a perfectly blackbody: e = 1. For a perfect reflector: e = 0.

cards.q: State Kirchhoff's Law of Radiation.
cards.a: At any given temperature, the ratio of emissive power to absorptive power is constant for all bodies and equals the emissive power of a perfectly blackbody (E / a = E_b ⇒ e = a).
cards.hint: Good absorbers are good emitters; poor absorbers are poor emitters.

cards.q: State the Stefan-Boltzmann Law for a blackbody and ordinary body.
cards.a:
Blackbody: R = E_b = σ T⁴ (radiant energy emitted per unit area per second).
Ordinary body: R = e σ T⁴.
Total power emitted: P = dQ/dt = e σ A T⁴.
cards.hint: Stefan's constant: σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/(m²·K⁴), dimensions: [M¹ L⁰ T⁻³ K⁻⁴].

cards.q: Net rate of heat loss of a body at temperature T in surroundings at T₀ (T > T₀)?
cards.a:
dQ / dt = e σ A (T⁴ - T₀⁴).
Rate of cooling (fall in temperature): -dT / dt = [ e σ A (T⁴ - T₀⁴) ] / (m c).
cards.hint: Temperatures T and T₀ MUST strictly be in KELVIN (absolute scale), never in Celsius!

cards.q: State Wien's Displacement Law.
cards.a: λ_max · T = b = constant, where λ_max is the wavelength of maximum spectral emissive power and T is absolute temperature.
cards.hint: Wien's constant: b ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K. As temperature increases, λ_max shifts towards shorter wavelengths (blue/UV).

cards.q: If absolute temperature of a blackbody is doubled, how do emissive power and peak wavelength change?
cards.a:
Emissive power: Increases by factor of 2⁴ = 16 times (R ∝ T⁴).
Peak wavelength λ_max: Halves (λ_max ∝ 1/T).
cards.hint: Classic MHT-CET MCQ! R becomes 16R, λ_max becomes λ/2.

cards.q: Newton's Law of Cooling: Formula and condition of validity?
cards.a:
dθ / dt = - k (θ - θ₀), where θ is body temperature, θ₀ is surroundings temperature, and k is cooling constant.
Integrated form: ln[(θ₁ - θ₀) / (θ₂ - θ₀)] = k t.
cards.hint: Valid ONLY when temperature difference (θ - θ₀) is small (less than ~30 °C) and heat loss is mainly by convection.

cards.q: Ferry's Blackbody: Key construction features?
cards.a:
Double-walled hollow spherical metal sphere with a narrow aperture and a conical projection directly opposite to the aperture.
Inner surface coated with lampblack (absorbs 96-98%), evacuated space between walls prevents conduction/convection.
cards.hint: Any ray entering suffers multiple internal reflections and is 100% absorbed. The aperture acts as the blackbody, NOT the wall.

cards.q: Adiabatic expansion: Relation between T and V for an ideal gas?
cards.a:
T V^(γ - 1) = constant.
Also: P V^γ = constant, and T^γ P^(1 - γ) = constant.
cards.hint: When gas expands adiabatically (V increases), its temperature T must DECREASE (cooling effect).

cards.q: At what temperature does the RMS speed of gas molecules become double its value at 0 °C?
cards.a:
T₂ = 1092 K = 819 °C.
Since v_rms ∝ √T: v₂ / v₁ = √(T₂ / T₁) = 2 ⇒ T₂ = 4 T₁ = 4 × 273 K = 1092 K = 819 °C.
cards.hint: Trap: You must convert 0 °C to 273 K first before multiplying by 4!

cards.q: What is the physical meaning of Absolute Zero (0 K)?
cards.a: The temperature at which translational kinetic energy of gas molecules becomes zero (v_rms = 0), and molecular motion theoretically ceases.
cards.hint: Pressure and volume of an ideal gas also extrapolate to zero at 0 K (-273.15 °C).

cards.q: Specific heat of a gas mixture of n₁ moles (C_v1) and n₂ moles (C_v2)?
cards.a:
C_v,mix = (n₁ C_v1 + n₂ C_v2) / (n₁ + n₂)
C_p,mix = (n₁ C_p1 + n₂ C_p2) / (n₁ + n₂)
γ_mix = C_p,mix / C_v,mix.
cards.hint: Weighted average based on number of moles.

cards.q: Greenhouse Effect: Which radiation is trapped?
cards.a: Short-wavelength solar radiation passes through atmosphere/glass, warms the Earth, which re-emits LONG-wavelength INFRARED radiation. Greenhouse gases (CO₂, H₂O, CH₄) absorb this infrared, trapping heat.
cards.hint: Glass/atmosphere is transparent to incoming visible/near-IR light, but opaque to outgoing long-wave thermal IR.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: If pressure of a gas is doubled at constant temperature, what happens to RMS speed?
cards.a:
v_rms remains COMPLETELY UNCHANGED!
Since v_rms = √(3 P / ρ) = √(3 R T / M₀), at constant temperature T, doubling P also doubles density ρ, so the ratio P/ρ stays constant.
cards.hint: v_rms depends ONLY on temperature and molar mass, NOT on pressure or volume alone!
